notes: Edinburgh International Accents of English Corpus (EdAcc) test split, 929 rows — accent-stress eval: dyadic Zoom conversations spanning 25 accent categories and 29 L1 backgrounds (top: Scottish English, Mainstream US English, Spanish-L1, Catalan-L1, Eastern European, Chinese). Tagged en-GB as the closest defensible BCP-47 code (UK-institution corpus, Edinburgh-collected, largest single accent bucket is Scottish English) — it is NOT a British-only accent set, most speakers are non-native or non-UK English speakers; per-row `accent`/`raw_accent`/`l1` columns exist in the source but this registry entry does not filter on them, so scores here measure robustness to accent diversity broadly, not specifically UK English. See PR notes. ~2% of rows (16/929 in the sampled shard) carry the STM out-of-bounds sentinel reference 'IGNORE_TIME_SEGMENT_IN_SCORING' instead of real transcript text; runner/stt_bench.py's STTBench.iter_samples filters these out (see _SENTINEL_REFERENCES) so they never enter a fighter's WER numerator/denominator. Other short/all-caps values in the corpus (YEAH, MM HMM, <OVERLAP>, <LAUGH>, ...) are genuine transcribed content/annotations, not sentinels, and are left unfiltered.
